issues.problem: Each tap starts its own Task running settings.set. Nothing serializes them. CommandBus.execute awaits hooks and gateway.authorize. If a plugin hook on settings.set suspends, a tap on Calm and then Off can land in the reverse order. The stored value then ends up Calm, which is not what the user picked last. The pending-token logic only hides this until both writes finish.
issues.fix: Chain the writes. Keep `private var lastWrite: Task<NibError?, Never>?`, and have commit await `lastWrite?.value` before calling bus.execute. Alternatively, skip a commit whose token is no longer `pending?.token` before executing. Add a test that fires two selections back to back and asserts the stored value is the last one.

issues.problem: LiquidChoice duplicates NibDesign's NibLiquidMode (full, calm, off). The test only claims they match and never checks it. LiquidChoice(setting:) also trims and lowercases the stored value. The consumers on feat/F016 (ToolbarView) and feat/F017 (DocumentContainerViewController) use the strict `NibLiquidMode(rawValue:) ?? .full`. So a stored " Calm" or "OFF" shows as Calm/Off on this page while the droplets run Full.
issues.fix: Build the control on NibLiquidMode itself, with an internal `extension NibLiquidMode { var title: String }` and `NibLiquidMode(rawValue:) ?? .full`. Or at minimum drop the trim and lowercase so the page reads the value the way the chrome does. Add `XCTAssertEqual(LiquidChoice.allCases.map(\.rawValue), NibLiquidMode.allCases.map(\.rawValue))`.

issues.problem: Three things in the failure path of the only user action have no test: clearing the pending choice, the control reverting, and posting .nibCommandFailed for the shell toast.
issues.fix: Register a Harness command hook for settings.set that throws, or pass an app whose settings.set is rejected. Call `await model.set(.off)` and assert the returned error is non-nil and `model.liquid` is back to the stored value. Also assert a .nibCommandFailed notification was posted with command == CommandIDs.settingsSet.

issues.problem: The run-time 'UI follows system' check looks only at each window and its root view controller. A presented controller, such as a settings sheet, a panel or a full-screen presentation, or a child controller that pins overrideUserInterfaceStyle, is never reported.
issues.fix: Walk each root's presentedViewController chain and its children recursively, and collect every controller's overrideUserInterfaceStyle. Add a windowFindings case for a presented controller in the tests.
